title_ar: شرح نخبة الفكر في مصطلح أهل الأثر الشريط التاسع -الخاتمة
title_en: Commentary on Nukhbat al-Fikr on the terminology of the people of hadith — tape nine, the conclusion
body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، اللهم صل وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد عبدك ونبيك ورسولك النبي الأمي وعلى آله وصحبه وسلم تسليما، قال المؤلف رحمه الله: «خاتمة» قد انتهى المؤلف رحمه الله من مصطلح الحديث بالمعنى الأخص، وبدأ في ذكر بعض علوم الحديث المستقلة وهي علوم أخرى يستحق كل واحد منها أن يدرس في دورة مستقلة، وقد ألفت فيها كتب كاملة، وهذه العلوم الأخرى منها علم الرجال والجرح والتعديل، ومنها علم التخريج، ومنها علم العلل، ومنها علم دراسة الأسانيد، وغير ذلك من العلوم المستقلة..
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. O God, bless and grant peace and blessing to our master Muhammad, Your servant and Your prophet and Your messenger, the unlettered Prophet, and to his family and his Companions, and grant them abundant peace.

The author, may God have mercy on him, said: "Conclusion." The author, may God have mercy on him, has finished with the terminology of hadith in its narrowest sense, and has begun to mention some of the independent hadith sciences. These are further sciences, each one of which deserves to be studied in a course of its own, and complete books have been written on them. Among these further sciences are the science of the narrators and their appraisal (al-jarḥ wa-l-taʿdīl); the science of tracing a report to its sources (takhrīj); the science of the hidden defects of reports (ʿilal); the science of the study of chains of transmission; and others besides among the independent sciences..

flags.context: the list of independent hadith sciences
options: the science of the hidden defects of reports (ʿilal)
the science of the defects of hadith
flags.note: The glossary fixes ʿillah as 'operative cause', which is its sense in legal theory and expressly not 'reason' or 'wisdom'. In the hadith sciences ʿilal is a different word with a different sense entirely: a subtle, hidden flaw in a chain or text that is not apparent on the surface. Option 2 would import the legal-theory sense and make nonsense of the list. The glossary should be extended with this second sense, as it will recur throughout the hadith material in this corpus.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

This record belongs to the Sheikh's commentary on Ibn Hajar al-ʿAsqalani's Nukhbat al-Fikr, a short manual of hadith terminology. The CMS holds the tapes out of order across ids 628–637 and the tape numbers in the titles do not run with the ids; the series should be ordered by the tape number in the title, not by id, and even then a gap remains (see the note on the download filenames).

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text is the opening of a lecture and breaks off; the full transcript is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.
'The author' throughout is Ibn Hajar al-ʿAsqalani, the author of the Nukhbah. He is not named in this excerpt.
'In its narrowest sense' renders bi-l-maʿnā al-akhaṣṣ — hadith terminology proper, as against the wider family of hadith sciences he is about to list.
'The unlettered Prophet' renders al-nabī al-ummī, part of the formula of prayer upon the Prophet and not a claim being advanced in the lesson.
The opening formula of prayer is a recited text; the Arabic is the operative form and is kept alongside the English rendering of its meaning.
